marks: Warden — an SRE agent for long-running compute jobs
A live machine is not correct training. Finished is not intact.
Warden was handed a spec. It is building the machine on Compute Engine right now.
Running: a Spot machine, a real model, heartbeats every few seconds
At step 600 this run hits a GPU out-of-memory error. Nobody is watching it.
It died. Warden opened an incident within one tick.
Evidence first — the failing line, quoted from the run's own log
Then the diagnosis. Every quote is checked against the raw log before anything is allowed to happen.
Warden decided by itself: resume at half the batch size. No human was asked.
Then it checks the world: did the new run actually pass the step it died at?
Past step 600 on the resumed run. The incident closes on evidence, not on an API returning OK.
Some actions Warden may not take alone. Those stop and wait for a person.
Every request carries what it will touch, what it costs, and when it lapses
Approved by the operator — and executed under the same policy as everything Warden does alone
The disk actually grew. Warden checked the machine, not the API's answer.
Every intent and every result is written down — including approvals answered from a phone in Discord
Warden cannot delete anything. That is denied by an IAM condition, not by good intentions.
And one button stops all of it
Frozen. Warden still watches and still proposes, but acts on nothing.
A live machine is not correct training. Finished is not intact. Warden watches the work.
